body:
**Adversarial review, round 1** on `a47131f` by claude-opus-5-5 (builder: claude-sonnet-5-5).

Request changes. The history endpoint matches the spec and app/openapi.yaml on shape, inclusive bounds, the 7-day limit (> 7 days rejected, exactly 7 days accepted), the empty result and the 404 for unknown sensors. One blocker: the sensor lookup reads inherited object keys, so `/sensors/__proto__/history` (also `constructor` and `toString`) throws inside the request handler and takes the server down. These ids should get 404 unknown_sensor. The fix should cover the `latest` handler too, which uses the same lookup and wrongly answers 200 for these ids. Low severity: FR-006 is listed as covered, but no test actually checks openapi.yaml.

- **F-1** [high] Prototype-key sensor id crashes the server (unauthenticated DoS) instead of returning 404 — `app/src/server.ts:19`
  `readings` is a plain object literal (app/src/data.ts:15), so `readings[history[1]]` also finds inherited keys. On `GET /sensors/__proto__/history?from=...&to=...` the lookup returns `Object.prototype`, and for `/sensors/constructor/history` or `/sensors/toString/history` it returns a function. In each case `!list` is false, so `list.filter` is called on something that has no `filter` and throws a TypeError. The throw happens synchronously inside the `createServer` request callback and there is no try/catch or `uncaughtException` handler, so the Node process exits. Any client can stop the service with one request. Under FR-003 these ids are unknown sensors and must get 404 `{ "error": "unknown_sensor" }`. Fix: check `Object.hasOwn(readings, id)`, or make `readings` a `Map` or `Object.create(null)`. Apply the same check to the existing `latest` lookup at line 13. It has the same flaw: today `/sensors/__proto__/latest` answers 200 `{ sensorId: '__proto__' }` instead of 404. If the fix only touches `history`, `latest` stays broken. Add a case covering it, for example asserting that `/sensors/__proto__/history` returns 404.
- **F-2** [low] FR-006 is claimed as covered, but no case checks openapi.yaml — `app/cases/1/history.spec.ts:1`
  The case manifest lists FR-006 (history documented in app/openapi.yaml with the response schema plus the 400 and 404 errors) as covered by app/cases/1/history.spec.ts. None of the tests in that file reads or validates app/openapi.yaml; they only exercise the HTTP behaviour. The openapi entry exists today (lines 22-44) and matches the spec, but if it is later removed or changed, no test will fail. Either add an assertion that parses openapi.yaml and checks that the `/sensors/{id}/history` GET has 200 (History), 400 (Error) and 404 (Error) responses, or remove FR-006 from the coverage claim.


Only @dharishan04 can close a finding without a fix: `/dismiss <F-n> <reason>`.
